observations: Photo 0 shows a black PlayStation 4 console and two grey DualShock 4 controllers on a blue plastic chair.
The console has visible scratches and scuffs on the top surface and sides.
The controllers appear to be standard DualShock 4 models, with no visible damage.
The console is placed upright, with the disc drive visible on the right side.
The background is a concrete wall, and the chair has minor wear and scratches.
There is a watermark 'MISHA JEREMIAH' across the image.

claims.claim: PS4 Fat Double Pad Good Condition
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the console and controllers, but no close-up of the console's ports or internal components. The 'Fat' model is not visible; the console appears to be the standard PS4 Slim or original model. The 'Double Pad' is supported by the presence of two controllers. 'Good Condition' is subjective and not verifiable from the photo alone.

claims.claim: Neatly used, never opened or repaired, no overheating, all ports working. Comes with the original pads and the UK receipt.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: Console may not be functional or may have internal damage (e.g., disc drive, HDMI, power issues).
risks.proof: A video showing the console powering on, loading a game, and connecting to a TV or monitor.

risks.risk: Controllers may be non-functional or have dead buttons/axes.
risks.proof: A video showing both controllers connecting to the console and responding to button presses.

risks.risk: Console may be a counterfeit or rebranded unit.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the console's serial number and model label, and a video of the console booting up with the official PS4 logo.

proof_requests: Close-up of the sticker with the model number, usually inside the original box.
Video of the console powering on and playing a game.
Video of both controllers connecting and working with the console.
Close-up photo of the console's serial number and model label.
Photo of the console's ports (HDMI, USB, power) to check for damage or corrosion.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
